intro_html: Zha jiang mian is Beijing comfort food, and it is built exactly the way a meal prepper would design it if you handed them the job. You make one pot of thick, salty, savory brown pork sauce. It sits in the fridge and gets better. Noodles go under it, cool raw cucumber and carrot go on top, and that hot-and-crunchy contrast is the whole point of the dish. If you have had dan dan noodles, this is not that. No sesame, no chili oil, just deep fermented flavor that tastes like it took all day.
cost_closing_html: About $3.15 a bowl (at everyday cost) for a noodle dinner with real pork shoulder in it, which is roughly what a single side order costs at the place down the street.
shop_smart: Pork shoulder is the cheapest honest cut in the case. It is fatty on purpose, and that fat is what makes this sauce taste rich without a drop of cream. Buy it whole and dice it yourself instead of paying for pre-cut.

Hoisin does the heavy lifting here. The traditional sauce leans on two fermented bean pastes most stores do not carry, and hoisin plus soy gets you to the same salty-sweet place from one jar that lasts many batches.
Cucumber and carrot are the cheapest things in this cart. Do not skip them thinking they are garnish. The raw crunch against the hot sauce is doing real work.
Cook the noodles the day you eat them if you can. Store the sauce on its own and boil a portion fresh, and the texture holds up far better than a pre-mixed container.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Dice the pork shoulder small, roughly pea-sized, so it eats like a sauce rather than a stew.
Heat the vegetable oil in a heavy pot and cook the pork over medium-high heat until it browns and renders its fat.
Add the garlic, ginger, and the white parts of the green onions and cook until fragrant.
Stir in the hoisin sauce and soy sauce and let them fry in the fat for a minute, which is what takes the raw edge off.
Pour in the chicken broth, drop the heat to low, and simmer uncovered until the sauce is thick and glossy and the pork is tender.
Boil the lo mein noodles to just tender, drain, and rinse briefly so they do not clump.
Cut the cucumber and carrots into matchsticks, then serve the sauce over the noodles with the raw vegetables and the green onion tops piled on.
portion_html: Put the full sauce pot on the scale, subtract the empty-pot weight from Step 1, and divide by 14. Weigh the same amount of cooked noodles into each container, spoon the sauce over, and tuck the cucumber and carrot in last so they stay crisp. Every serving comes in at 598 calories with 25 grams of protein.
upsell_html: Deep, savory dinners for about $3.15 a bowl (at everyday cost). This is one of many. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons, calculators, and tools, all for $1 a month.

steps: Dice the pork shoulder small and brown it in hot oil until the fat renders.
Add garlic, ginger, and green onion whites and cook until fragrant.
Fry the hoisin and soy sauce in the fat, then pour in the broth.
Simmer uncovered until the sauce is thick and the pork is tender.
Boil the lo mein noodles and cut the cucumber and carrots into matchsticks.
Portion noodles into 14 containers, then top with sauce and raw vegetables.
